Clashing Tides In The Tasman Sea

Rohan Daswani

Gavekal Research | 19 Nov 2026

For decades, the Australian and New Zealand dollars have moved broadly in tandem against the US dollar, reflecting their shared exposure to global commodity demand, particularly from China. Australia’s exports are dominated by metals and energy, while New Zealand specializes in agricultural products such as dairy and meat. Recently, however, the two currencies have moved in opposite directions as diverging monetary policy expectations and economic prospects have broken their traditional relationship.Strong demand for key Australian commodity exports, including coal and liquefied natural gas, together with a more hawkish central bank, has supported the Australian dollar. Meanwhile, New Zealand has struggled with weaker domestic growth, high unemployment and households still feeling the effects of a prolonged post-Covid property slump. The country’s sluggish recovery from the pandemic has also encouraged its citizens to seek better job opportunities and health care in Australia, adding to the New Zealand dollar’s relative weakness.
